Subject: SIG Q15 / Q74 clarification — key rotation and backup access

Diego — thanks for sending the draft SIG. Our security reviewers flagged two items that need clearer answers before we can move to procurement: Q15 (Key management: who can access raw key material used for backups) and Q74 (Backups: encryption + key rotation responsibilities). The spreadsheet has our inline notes (attached: ClearWave_SIG_questions_v3.xlsx).

High level asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether any Redwood personnel or partner (e.g., infra ops, support engineers) can access customer encryption keys or plaintext backups?
- If we rely on a cloud KMS, who is responsible for rotating backup keys and what's the expected rotation cadence?

We would like a short written response ahead of the call next week; our security team will use that to scope evidence requests.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: SIG Q15 / Q74 clarification — key rotation and backup access

Alicia — thanks for the clear notes and the spreadsheet. Quick summary before we put formal language into the SIG response:

1) Raw key material: Redwood never persists customer raw encryption keys. For our Hosted and Dedicated offerings we integrate with customer-managed KMS or our recommended KMS provider; we only store key references (key IDs) and ciphertext.

2) Access controls: No Redwood support or infra engineer has the ability to retrieve customer plaintext keys or access unencrypted backup contents. Access to KMS for operations is strictly via customer-owned keys and limited IAM roles; we can provide role lists and a sample least-privileged IAM policy.

3) Key rotation: Responsibility depends on config:
- Customer-managed KMS: customer rotates keys per their policy (we provide guidance).
- Redwood-managed KMS (rare / contracted): Redwood performs automated rotation every 90 days by default; rotation is auditable and we keep KMS rotation logs.

We can provide:
- A short written interpretation for Q15 and Q74 for your SIG,
- Excerpts of KMS audit logs (redacted) as evidence,
- A sample IAM policy and RBAC roles.

Would you like us to treat the answers in the spreadsheet as "Redwood-proposed" so you can mark them up, or do you prefer we push a final response directly into the Excel?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Diego / Neha — following up with the security engineering interpretation I promised on the call scheduling. A few technical clarifications to make the SIG answers unambiguous:

- Q15 (key access): The SIG wording "access raw key material" is ambiguous because some vendors interpret "access" to include key identifiers or wrapped keys. For audit clarity, propose we answer with two bullets:
  a) We do not store or have access to customer plaintext keys or unencrypted backups.
  b) We may store wrapped keys / key identifiers required for runtime; those are not usable without the customer KMS.

- Q74 (backup rotation): The SIG asks who performs rotation and at what cadence. We should state default behavior and note exceptions:
  • If customer brings their own KMS (BYOK), rotation is customer-controlled and Redwood recommends >=90-day rotation.
  • For Redwood-managed KMS, rotation interval = 90 days; emergency rotation procedures documented with SLA.

Evidence we can attach: redacted KMS rotation logs (sample), IAM role list, and the config snippet showing rotation automation. I will prepare a one-page memo for the SIG response and a redacted log excerpt (pdf).

Mina Haddad
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Alicia / team — thanks for the call Friday and for the follow-up questions. Below is the agreed wording we will paste into the SIG spreadsheet (and we attached the redacted logs). Please confirm you are happy and we'll upload the final Excel to your portal.

Agreed SIG responses (Q15 / Q74):

Q15 — Key material access
- Redwood does not persist customer plaintext encryption keys or unencrypted backup contents.
- For runtime we store wrapped keys and key identifiers required to reference customer keys; wrapped keys are unusable outside the KMS without the customer key material.
- Redwood personnel do not possess credentials that would allow unwrapping customer keys; privileged access is controlled via IAM and audited.

Q74 — Backup encryption and rotation responsibilities
- If customer uses customer-managed KMS (BYOK): rotation is customer responsibility; Redwood documents recommended cadence (>=90 days) and provides tooling guidance.
- If Redwood-managed KMS is contracted: Redwood performs automated rotation on a 90-day cadence by default and will provide monthly rotation reports and rotation logs on request per the contract. Emergency rotation procedures are available in our runbook.

Deliverables attached:
- Redwood_kms_audit_excerpt.pdf (redacted rotation logs)
- ClearWave_SIG_questions_v3_final.xlsx (finalized SIG answers) — will upload directly to your portal once you confirm.
